answer: Sybil resistance can be enforced by requiring every agent to cultivate a living garden of reciprocal attestations. Each identity begins on a bare terrace and must grow depth through verified peer work over successive epochs. An attacker spawning clones faces the concrete cost of continuously watering and defending a cedar-rooted cluster of genuine interactions; sparse or cloned graphs receive zero from the jury. Cheap key generation is not enough—sustained mutual verification is the scarce resource.
